# Host-wide release barrier: pause new implement/audit dispatch on every root while a release runs

## Problem statement

The Code Freeze marker (`.worklog/code-freeze.json`) is **per worklog root**, while the host dispatch budget ledger in `~/.herdr/downtime/` is **machine-scoped**. During a release in project A the dispatcher therefore pauses new implement/audit dispatch for project A only; a second project on the same host — or the coordination leader's registered-root sweep — can still start implement and audit panes exactly while the release's own audit/test subprocesses are saturating the machine. The residual risk is host-level contention (OOM, CPU starvation, contended slot budgets) caused by work that a release should have paused.

## Users

- **Operator/Producer running a release** — *As an operator shipping project A, I expect that starting a release pauses new heavy (implement/audit) dispatch everywhere on this machine, not just in the project being released, so the release's own audit and test runs are not competing with freshly started panes.*
- **Downtime dispatcher (agent)** — *As the dispatcher on a root that is not being released, I need an unambiguous, stable reason for why I am not starting implement/audit work, so I keep polling instead of arming the no-candidate cooldown and instead of retrying the same blocked work every tick.*
- **Author of work in another project on the host** — *As an agent whose implement work is paused host-wide, I want plan/intake prep to keep flowing and in-progress panes to be left alone, so a long release does not become a full work stoppage or kill work already under way.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Host-scoped barrier is honoured on every root.** While a release is running anywhere on the host, every worklog root on that host refuses **new** implement and audit dispatch — both the instance's own-backlog/offer path and the coordination leader's registered-root sweep — regardless of whether that root has its own code-freeze marker. The barrier decision is re-read fresh on every dispatch tick (never cached across ticks).
- **Distinct neutral reason token.** A skip caused by the host barrier reports a dedicated terminal reason (proposed `host-release-barrier`) that is **never** `no-candidate`, so the no-candidate cooldown does not arm and dispatch resumes on the first tick after the barrier lifts. The token is added to the terminal-reason union, the offer-gate / empty-offer vocabulary, the header/log token mapping, and the reason-token table in the dispatcher docs.
- **Running work is untouched; prep still flows.** In-progress implement/audit panes are never interrupted, terminated or paused by the barrier; plan and intake dispatch (including critical prep) continues normally, matching the per-root freeze split-by-skill rule.
- **Per-root gate retained and composed.** The existing per-root code-freeze gate stays in place and composes with the host barrier as belt-and-braces: either signal alone pauses implement/audit for that root. Precedence is pinned by tests (a root's own freeze reports the per-root `code-freeze` token; the host token is reported when only the host barrier explains the skip).
- **A dead release cannot stall the host forever.** A barrier signal left behind by a release that was killed hard (SIGKILL / OOM / reboot, so its cleanup never ran) must stop barring dispatch — the pid-liveness plus grace-period rule already established for the per-root marker (SA-0MSDX3EYZ005SGIK) applies to the barrier decision. An untrustworthy (unreadable/corrupt) barrier signal is treated as active (fail-closed for dispatch) only for as long as that staleness rule allows.
- **Budget accounting is unchanged.** The host dispatch-budget ledger's admission path (`admitHostDispatch` and the count/reduce helpers) is untouched: the barrier is a separate, earlier gate that skips dispatch without taking, releasing or reserving a budget slot.
- **Tests pin the behaviour.** New/extended automated tests cover: barrier active on a root with no marker of its own (own-backlog path); barrier active during a registered-root sweep; per-root freeze still honoured when the host barrier is absent; plan/intake still dispatch while barred; in-progress panes untouched; stale/dead-release signal stops barring; neutral token never becomes `no-candidate`. Tests assert observable dispatch outcomes via the public dispatch contract, not source greps.
- **Documentation is updated** to reflect the change: the dispatcher reference (gate table, filter-chain position, reason tokens, machine-dir files) and the release-window evaluation note that spawned this item, including the code comments in the touched modules.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Impact

While a release runs anywhere on the machine, no other project on that host starts new implement or audit panes, so a release stops competing with freshly dispatched agent work for CPU, memory and model slots.

## Constraints

- **Implement and audit only** (including their critical variants, per the existing split-by-skill rule); plan/intake/risk-effort prep behaviour is whatever the existing per-root freeze already does — the barrier must not invent a second, divergent tier table.
- **Admission gate only** — never terminate, pause or hijack a running pane.
- **Single machine**, matching the existing ledger and coordination dir; no cross-machine (flock/NFS) coordination is introduced, and no proxy/HTTP signal is required.
- **Fail directions:** absent signal ⇒ no barrier; unreadable/ambiguous signal ⇒ barrier active, bounded by the staleness rule.
- **No new budget slot** — the evaluation in WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3 explicitly rejected a dedicated release budget slot; this item must not reintroduce one.
- **Insertion point:** immediately beside the existing code-freeze gate (before budget admission), so the filter-chain order and every downstream gate stay as documented.
- **herdr owns the reading.** Nothing in this item changes how a release writes its own per-root marker unless the producer chooses the dedicated-marker mechanism (see Open question 1).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — per-root marker reader with fail-open (`readCodeFreezeState`/`isCodeFreezeActive`) and tri-state fail-closed (`readCodeFreezeStatus` → `frozen`/`not-frozen`/`ambiguous`) semantics, plus `readCodeFreezeStatusForRoot(root)` and atomic `writeCodeFreezeMarker`/`clearCodeFreezeMarker`. **No staleness/pid-liveness check exists in this module** — a marker with `active: true` is trusted indefinitely.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` (~line 460) — the tick-level read: `const freezeStatus = deps.readCodeFreezeStatus(opts.cwd); const frozen = freezeStatus === 'frozen' || freezeStatus === 'ambiguous';`. This single `frozen` value wraps the audit tier, the non-critical implement tier, the review-queue read, the scheduled-prompt path and the stalled-resume scan, and is threaded into `dispatchFromHerdrList` as `ctx.frozen`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` (~line 469) — the registered-root sweep recomputes `frozen` per root (tick-level read for `opts.cwd`, fresh `readCodeFreezeStatus(root)` for every other registered root) and passes it into `dispatchFromOwnHead`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — `selectCriticalFirstCandidates(items, now, frozen)` applies the split-by-skill rule (skips audit/implement/risk-effort candidates while frozen) on the Herdr-head paths.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` / `.coordination-leader.ts` — the offer path rejects an offer with the `'code-freeze'` gate token at the equivalent position in its filter sequence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` / `.offer-attribution.ts` / `.constants.ts` — the terminal-reason union, the offer-gate token union and the empty-offer reason union, plus the header token mapping. A new token must be added in all of these or the skip will be mis-labelled.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — resolves the machine coordination dir (`HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` or `~/.herdr/downtime`), owns the host dispatch-budget ledger and the retired `active-audit` read. Header documents the single-machine scope.
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` — the precedent for a machine-scoped marker: versioned on-disk contract, atomic temp+rename write, tolerant read where `[]` (nothing recorded) and `null` (cannot read) are deliberately distinguishable.
- `deps.readCodeFreezeStatus` is an injected dependency on the dispatch deps contract, so a barrier read must be injected the same way to stay testable without touching the real machine dir.
- Release side (SorraAgents repo, out of this repo but load-bearing for the contract): `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (`setCodeFreezeMarker`/`clearCodeFreezeMarker`, `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`) and `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` (bash write + `EXIT` trap clear); `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` already implements pid-liveness + 15-minute grace staleness (SA-0MSDX3EYZ005SGIK) — herdr's TypeScript reader does not.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the canonical gate table, filter-chain order and reason-token list (the "Freeze is per root" paragraph is the sentence this item changes). `docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md` — the evaluation that identified this gap.

## Desired change

Read one host-scoped barrier state **once per dispatch tick** and fold it into the existing `frozen` predicate at its three computation sites (`dispatch.ts` tick level, `head-scan.ts` per root, and wherever `ctx.frozen` is consumed), so the barrier needs no tier table of its own: `frozen = rootFrozen || hostBarrier`. Report the new neutral reason token when only the host barrier explains a skip, keep `code-freeze` precedence for a root's own marker, add the staleness rule for the barrier decision, and pin every behaviour with tests and docs. The budget ledger is not touched; the barrier sits immediately before/alongside the existing freeze gate.

**Open question 1** (mechanism — affects files and repos but not the observable ACs): where does the host-scoped signal come from?

- **(a) Derived** — treat the host as barred when **any** registered root's existing per-root `code-freeze.json` is frozen/ambiguous. No new file, no cross-repo writer change, no second marker contract to keep in sync, and every existing release path (ship skill *and* the herdr Ship-It confirmation writer) is automatically covered. Reads are one small JSON file per registered root per tick; reach equals `downtimeWorklogRoots` reach.
- **(b) Dedicated machine marker** — a new machine-scoped marker in the coordination dir (e.g. `~/.herdr/downtime/release-barrier.json`), written/cleared by the release process with the same atomic + fail-closed semantics as `code-freeze.json`. Semantically the most precise and independent of a roots list, but it needs a sibling SorraAgents work item (the ship skill is the writer of record), duplicates path resolution in a second repo/language, and a release path that forgets to write it silently loses the barrier.

**Recommended: (a) derived** — it closes exactly the observed gap with no new cross-repo contract and inherits all existing writers; the staleness rule must then be added to the herdr read used by the barrier.

**Open question 2** (staleness): adopt SA-0MSDX3EYZ005SGIK's rule (probe the recorded `pid`; a dead pid older than a 15-minute grace from `startedAt` means stale) for the barrier decision only, or for every herdr code-freeze read (also closing the latent per-root hole)? **Recommended: every read** — one rule, one place, and the barrier multiplies the blast radius of an expiring-never marker from one project to the whole machine.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — add the barrier read (or a `readHostReleaseBarrier()` helper) and the staleness rule; keep the existing fail-open/tri-state contracts intact.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine coordination dir plumbing / marker path constants if the dedicated-marker mechanism is chosen; the barrier read belongs beside the budget ledger.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — fold the host barrier into the tick-level `frozen` computation and report the new neutral reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — fold the host barrier into the per-root `frozen` used by the registered-root sweep.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — split-by-skill rule now applies on `rootFrozen || hostBarrier` (no new tier table).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` / `.coordination-leader.ts` — offer-path rejection + gate token for the barrier.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` — terminal-reason union gains the barrier token.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — offer-gate / empty-offer vocabulary + dominant-gate mapping.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — header/decision token mapping for the new reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts` — inject the barrier read on the dispatch deps (same seam style as `readCodeFreezeStatus`).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — gate table, "Freeze is per root" paragraph, reason-token list, machine-dir file inventory.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — the plugin-facing freeze/budget behaviour section (banner, blocked shortcuts, budget counters) gains the host barrier.
- `docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md` — record that residual gap 1 is closed by this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Host-wide stall from a stale signal** — the single worst failure mode: one dead release can freeze implement/audit on every project. Mitigated by the pid-liveness + grace staleness rule (AC5) and by the fact that the barrier is an admission gate only. Assumption: a *live* release longer than the grace period keeps its pid alive, so the barrier correctly holds.
- **Over-blocking is accepted by design** — a long release pauses implement/audit host-wide; that is the intent. It must be operator-visible (decision log + header token + docs) so it never looks like a broken dispatcher.
- **Divergent tier tables** — if the barrier grows its own list of paused tiers instead of reusing `frozen`, the two freeze mechanisms will drift. Assumption: reuse `frozen` verbatim.
- **Cross-repo contract drift** (mechanism (b) only) — path resolution and marker shape would exist in herdr TS, SorraAgents JS and SorraAgents Python. Mitigated by choosing (a), or by one documented contract plus contract tests.
- **Reach gap in mechanism (a)** — a root that is frozen but not listed in `downtimeWorklogRoots` does not bar the host. That is acceptable: dispatch reach equals registry reach, and that root's own tick already blocks on its own marker.
- **Inherited blind spot** — the coordination offer path writes offers before the leader evaluates them; the barrier gates the *dispatch* decision, not offer creation. Assumption: paused offers are re-offered next tick and the neutral token keeps the item visible.
- **Documentation collision** — WL-0MWF359A8005ZRF4 (blocked) rewrites the same two documents (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`) for the generalised budget. Sequence the doc edits after it, or keep this item's doc changes to the freeze/barrier sections to avoid a conflict.

# F2 — Generic admission + audit-only over-hold

Second implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: make admission one generic
path for every capped kind on BOTH dispatcher paths (direct and coordination
leader), keep the counting asymmetry audit-only (`freshCount` over-hold for
audit; `liveCount` live-pane release for every other kind), and unify refusal
tokens on `host-budget-<kind>` (removing the `maxAudit: 1` → `audit-host-saturated`
special-case). Uncapped kinds admit without reservation and touch no ledger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch` resolves the kind's cap from the generalised config:
  absent ⇒ admit WITHOUT reservation (no reserve/release/confirm bookkeeping);
  present ⇒ existing live-count admission; `0` ⇒ refuse with `0/0`.
- Counting asymmetry preserved: only `audit` uses `freshCount` (slot held from
  reservation until a release point or the 2 h stale window, no live-pane
  requirement); `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort` use `liveCount`
  (live-pane release, pane-derived freshness).
- Admission is enforced on BOTH dispatcher paths: the direct path
  (`dispatchClaimedTier` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`) and the
  coordination-leader path (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` /
  `coordination-batch.ts`) call the same generic `admitHostDispatch` for every
  capped kind and skip it for uncapped kinds.
- Refusal tokens unified: `host-budget-<kind>` for the kind's cap refusal;
  `audit-host-saturated` special-case removed (the audit tier reports
  `host-budget-audit` at every cap including the `maxAudit: 1` default).
- Fail-closed semantics unchanged: unreadable ledger ⇒ `host-budget-unknown` +
  repair from live panes; `no-coordination-dir` ⇒ admit; lock/IO failure ⇒ refuse.
- `kindOf`/`entriesFromLivePanes` reconstruct any kind's pane (not just
  implement/audit) for the repair path.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC1 — any kind configurable):** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the per-kind kill switch.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC4 — counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only):** only `audit` keeps the over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold, repair
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — admission choke
  point (`dispatchClaimedTier`) + failure release for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` —
  `dispatchFromCoordination` admission
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `admitHostDispatch` seam (kind passthrough)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.test.ts` /
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Generalise `admitHostDispatch` to look up the kind's cap/absence.
2. Add the no-reservation fast path for uncapped kinds.
3. Remove the `audit-host-saturated` special-case in `readAuditBudgetState` /
   `admitAuditLegacy`; unify on `host-budget-audit`.
4. Generalise `kindOf` / `entriesFromLivePanes` for pane-title reconstruction.
5. Widen `releaseHostBudgetForFailure` and the admission call in
   `dispatchClaimedTier` to all kinds (skip still for uncapped — release is a
   no-op for kinds that never reserve).
6. Update admission/dispatch/coordination tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F1 (WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88) — generalised config/ledger.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the test matrix pins admission semantics.

## Deliverables

One generic admission path; audit-only over-hold; unified tokens; both
dispatcher paths enforce caps for every configured kind.

data.description:
## Headline

A driven child's pre-push full-suite gate must judge only the mutation its own
run could have caused — currently a concurrent session's mid-run writes to the
shared main checkout are misattributed to the suite and block the push.

## Summary

A driven child's `implement.py finish` is refused when the pre-push full-suite
gate observes another live session's uncommitted edits in the **main checkout**.
The gate reports `live_repo_mutation` ("the test suite changed a guarded
checkout") and fails the run, so the push is refused — even though the child's
own worktree is clean and its commit is composed only of its own files.

Observed while finishing WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR (tests-only, worktree clean,
changed-scope green): the full-suite gate failed with

```text
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for .../worktrees/wl-WL-0MWETWFSH...
  in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub:
  added path [ M] docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.ts
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts
```

Evidence that the mutation is concurrent agent activity, not the suite:
`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts` has mtime 22:42:45,
four seconds *after* the suite started at 22:42:41, and the paths belong to the
host-dispatch-budget workstream (WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR, held by
`herdr-1794608223-1882173-11244`, driving children from ~22:17). No test in this
repo writes `.ts` sources.

## Users

- **Driven implementer agent (finishing a child in its worktree).** As an
  implementing agent I want my finish gate to judge only the mutation my own run
  could have caused, so I am not blocked by another session's unrelated work in
  the shared main checkout.
- **Operator / maintainer.** As an operator I want a gate failure to name the
  owning session or work item, so I know who is writing the checkout and do not
  hunt a phantom bug in a clean tree.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatcher I do not want a false gate failure
  to burn a retry slot or re-dispatch work that is already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate distinguishes changes that were pre-existing before the run, or made
  by another live session, from changes the suite made during this run, and
  fails the run only on the latter (the verdict is derived from a start-of-run
  snapshot of the guarded checkout, never from an unqualified `HEAD`/`git
  status` comparison).
- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate
  passed is not blocked by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout.
- When the gate does fail, the report names the owning session/work item where
  one is discoverable (e.g. via `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the
  main-checkout lock holder), instead of implying the running item corrupted the
  tree.
- A genuine suite-caused mutation of a guarded checkout — above all a
  tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout (the 2026-10-26
  `packages/shared` incident class) — still fails the run: the fix narrows the
  false positive without weakening that protection.
- Regression tests cover both directions: (a) a dirty main checkout with a clean
  child worktree ⇒ the gate passes and reports the foreign paths as
  informational; (b) the suite mutating the guarded checkout during the run ⇒
  the gate fails and names the paths.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop chasing a phantom corruption bug when a concurrent session has the
main checkout dirty, and driven children are no longer blocked by work they
never touched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking a real wipe.** Narrowing the main-checkout surface (option A)
  could let a suite-caused *addition* through. Mitigation: the deletion/wipe
  class (the actual incident) stays verdict-bearing, and the finish
  main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2CMY/CZ family) remains a second net.
- **Risk: actor attribution is unreliable.** Mid-run writes carry no ownership
  metadata git can read; probing `.implement_state.json`/claimed items is
  best-effort. Assumption: attribution is informational and always falls back to
  "unknown" rather than becoming a new failure mode.
- **Risk: pin/test churn.** Changing the clean→dirty direction moves a pinned
  characterisation test and a documented blind spot; the change must update
  rule, docs and pin together (see Constraints).
- **Risk: scope creep.** Options B/C expand into actor-attribution plumbing and
  isolated-worktree migration. Mitigation: keep this item to the false-positive
  verdict; record the isolated-worktree migration under WL-0MW4W15U500009D2 and
  any actor-attribution enhancement as separate linked work.
- **Assumption:** the guarded run's own worktree is the only checkout the suite
  can legitimately write; the main checkout is shared and may be written by
  other live sessions at any time.
- **Assumption:** "live session" is not directly observable; attribution uses
  whatever durable evidence exists (state files, claimed items, lock holder) and
  degrades to "unknown".

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the wipe protection.** The main-checkout coverage exists
  because a worktree-scoped suite wiped every tracked file of `packages/shared`
  on 2026-10-26 (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG). Tracked-file
  deletions in the main checkout must still fail the run.
- **Conflicting documented design decision.** The working-tree attribution rule
  (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5) **deliberately
  retains** the clean→dirty direction as a mutation, pinned by
  `TestWorkingTreeAttributionBoundaries::test_clean_to_dirty_is_a_retained_move_direction`
  and documented as blind spot #2. Any change to that direction must update the
  rule, the doc section and the pin together in one change.
- **Plumbing-only derivations.** The guard's derivations must stay git-plumbing
  only (status codes + the start snapshot) — never a `wl-*` or path-name
  heuristic. If actor evidence is introduced, it must be an explicit, documented
  second signal, not a substitute for the plumbing rule.
- **Exactly one guard owner.** `guarded_run_all` is the single outer guard owner;
  the inner `live_repo_guard` plugin must apply the same rule and must not fork
  it.
- **Bounded cost.** The guard stays read-only git plumbing with no per-test work
  (the per-test fingerprint remains a trigger, never a verdict).
- **Fail closed.** `implement.py finish` must never push a checkout that a
  suite-caused mutation corrupted; narrowing the false positive must not turn a
  genuine mutation green.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `guarded_run_all` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) snapshots every guarded
  root before the run (`snapshot_guarded_roots`: the worktree plus, when it is a
  linked worktree, its main checkout) and diffs afterwards
  (`diff_guarded_roots` → `diff_snapshots`). `_detect_live_repo_mutation` renders
  the verdict; `implement.py`'s finish gate delegates to `guarded_run_all` and
  classifies `live_repo_mutation` as `GATE_FAILURE_INFRASTRUCTURE`.
- Attribution is **start-of-run provenance**: a path that was dirty at start and
  clean at end is excluded and reported under `live_repo_excluded`; a path that
  was **clean at start and dirty at end** (`status.added`) or is still dirty with
  a different code (`status.changed`) fails the run.
- The observed failure is the **clean→dirty direction**: the concurrent session
  wrote `.ts` sources into the main checkout *during* the run (mtime four
  seconds after the suite started), so the start-of-run snapshot was clean and
  the end snapshot showed them as `added path`.
- A single-owner lock exists for the main checkout during **finish**
  (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84), but it does not stop a non-finish session (a driven
  child or the operator) writing the main checkout mid-run.
- A related alternative mitigation is already scoped: run the post-push/audit
  full suite in a pinned isolated worktree (WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, blocked; its
  tests in WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ, intake_complete).

## Desired change

**Outcome:** a driven child whose own worktree is clean is not blocked by another
live session's mid-run writes to the main checkout; a genuine suite-caused
mutation (especially a tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout) still
fails the run; and a failure names the owning session/work item when
discoverable.

**Mechanism is an open design question (Appendix Q1).** Candidate approaches
(not prescriptive — the plan stage must confirm):

- **(A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict surface** to the damage class the
  suite can plausibly cause — tracked-file **deletions** and modifications of
  files that were clean at start — and report concurrent **additions/untracked
  creations** as informational, naming the owning session where discoverable.
  Keeps the wipe protection, removes the dominant false positive.
- **(B) Keep the full status surface, add actor attribution** (owning session /
  work item from `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the main-checkout
  lock holder) and fail only when a change cannot be attributed to a foreign
  live session.
- **(C) Run the pre-push full-suite gate in an isolated worktree** pinned to the
  would-be-commit (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2), so main-checkout churn is
  out of scope entirely.
- **(D) Scope the verdict to the guarded root only** when the run started in a
  worktree, reporting main-checkout churn informationally — weakest option;
  regresses the 2026-10-26 protection, so not recommended.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`,
  `_detect_live_repo_mutation`, verdict → `live_repo_mutation` /
  `live_repo_excluded`.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `snapshot_guarded_roots`,
  `diff_guarded_roots`, `diff_snapshots` attribution rule,
  `describe_guarded_diff`, `excluded_churn_notes`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — inner pytest plugin; applies the same rule
  and must not fork it.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish test gate,
  `_adapt_guarded_result`, `_gate_failure_reason`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — `TestWorkingTreeAttribution*`
  pins; the clean→dirty pin must move with the rule.
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — outer-guard end-to-end tests
  (add the dirty-main/clean-worktree pass and the genuine-mutation fail).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 — attribution rule and blind spots.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish-gate and guard-ownership
  documentation.

## Related work

From `/skill:find-related` (automated report):

- **WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O** (completed) — added the main-checkout guard this
  item's false positive fires from.
- **WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q** (completed) — finish aborts loudly on foreign
  main-checkout deletions; already names the concurrent actor on the *finish*
  guard surface.
- **WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84** (completed) — single-owner lock for the main checkout
  during finish; does not cover non-finish writers.
- **WL-0MW4W15U500009D2** (blocked) — redirect post-push verification full-suite
  runs to a pinned isolated worktree; the architectural alternative to (C).
- **WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ** (intake_complete) — regression tests for the
  isolated-worktree verification run.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — the working-tree attribution rule (start-of-run
  provenance); the design decision this item asks to revisit for the
  clean→dirty direction.
- **WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR** — the concurrent host-dispatch-budget workstream whose
  writes triggered the observed failure.
- **WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR** (completed) — the driven child whose finish was
  blocked by the false positive.
- **WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U**, **WL-0MV981ZGA007ARPG** (completed) — the concurrent
  `dev`/`origin/*` ref-exclusion regressions that must stay green.
- Docs: `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — which attribution mechanism?** AC1's suggested
  mechanism ("compare against a start-of-run snapshot of the guarded checkout, not
  against `HEAD`") is **already implemented** in `guarded_run_all` /
  `diff_snapshots`. The observed failure is the clean→dirty direction — a foreign
  session wrote files into the main checkout *during* the run — which the
  documented rule (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `test-isolation.md` §8.5 blind spot #2)
  deliberately retains as a mutation and pins with a characterisation test. A pure
  start-of-run snapshot cannot tell a mid-run foreign write from a suite write.
  Which approach should the plan adopt?
  (A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict to tracked-file deletions/modifications
  and report concurrent additions informationally;
  (B) keep the full surface and add actor attribution;
  (C) move the gate to an isolated worktree pinned to the would-be-commit
  (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2);
  (D) guard only the worktree root (not recommended).
  **Recommended: (A)** — it keeps the 2026-10-26 deletion/wipe protection while
  removing the dominant false positive (concurrent additions/untracked files) at
  low plumbing-only cost; (C) is the strongest long-term fix but is a separate,
  already-scoped item.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.
- **Q2 — how much actor detail is required on failure?** AC2 requires naming the
  owning session/work item "where discoverable". Which evidence sources are
  acceptable? (a) `.implement_state.json` / claimed work items only;
  (b) add the main-checkout lock holder metadata; (c) best-effort plus
  "unknown".
  **Recommended: (c)** — best-effort from (a) and (b), falling back to
  "unknown", so attribution never becomes a new failure mode.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.
- **Q3 — should this item fold into the isolated-worktree item?** Option (C)
  largely duplicates WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, which is blocked. Should this item
  stay narrow (false-positive attribution on the live guard) and leave the
  isolated-worktree migration to that item?
  **Recommended: keep this item narrow** — it fixes the gate's verdict on
  today's live-checkout path; the isolated-worktree migration is a separate
  architectural change with its own regression tests.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.

## Summary

`implement.py finish` fast-forwards the local `dev` branch to the about-to-be-pushed tip **before** the push succeeds, and restores it on failure. A concurrent `implement.py start` that runs inside that window resolves `dev` to the unpushed commit and creates its worktree/branch from it — permanently grafting another item's commit onto the new branch.

Observed on 2026-11-13:

- WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's finish created commit `e2291be45` (tests-only) and moved local `dev` to it before its push gate failed; finish then restored `dev` to `079948694`.
- `git reflog show wl-WL-0MWFJDGXQ001OXP8-append-only-audit-trail-for-budget-ledge` shows a single entry: `e2291be45 … branch: Created from dev` — i.e. the sibling child's worktree was created from the transient, unpushed tip.
- That branch is now `[ahead 1]` of `dev` with a foreign commit as its base, so its first push to `dev` will carry WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's commit under the wrong item id (or dump both in one push).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `finish` never moves the local `dev` ref while a push is in flight; the post-push fast-forward happens only after `git push` reports success
- On a failed/refused push, local `dev` is provably unchanged from its pre-finish value (no write-then-restore window)
- `implement.py start` resolves its base from `origin/dev` (fetched) rather than a locally mutable `dev`, or refuses to branch from a `dev` that is not a known pushed tip
- Regression test: simulate a mid-push `start` and assert the new branch's base is the pushed tip, never an unpushed sibling commit
- Full test suite passes

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (finish push + dev sync; start base resolution)

## Impact

A new child's branch can no longer inherit another work item's unpushed commit, so each push to `dev` contains exactly the work item's own changes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MV5FDJE30088GGY** – implement.py finish: NameError 'cwd' in non-fast-forward rebase-retry path (completed)
- **WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M** – implement.py finish fails non-fast-forward when dev advances during the run (completed)
- **WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9** – Pre-push hook template: bind the full-suite gate to the pushed commit (--gate-commit) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mwfjdgxq001oxp8, acceptance, ahead, another, append (+91 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, ahead, another, append, assert (+91 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: acceptance, ahead, another, audit, base (+74 more)

# Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

> **Migrated** from the SorraAgents worklog item **SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS** (2026-11-13) after the producer approved migrating it here, accepting the re-scope and deleting the SorraAgents original. Provenance for the orphan census below is the SorraAgents worklog; the engineering scope is entirely in this repository.

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 SorraAgents backlog review)

55 of 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

`wl delete` is recursive by default (documented), and `--no-recursive` is the documented "leaving children orphaned" opt-out, but a hard delete evidently bypassed the children; the exact route that produced the 46-item batch is confirmed below as `wl doctor prune` / `foreign-items --apply` (see R1).

## Re-scope (producer-approved 2026-11-13)

Investigation of this repo (main @ `77264ee6a`) shows the original acceptance criteria are **substantially shipped**, which narrows the work:

- **Recursive delete ships.** `wl delete` is recursive by default, has an explicit `--no-recursive` opt-out, records `--reason`, and reports the deleted descendants — `src/commands/delete.ts` (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- **Doctor already flags orphans.** Root `wl doctor` (`validate`) emits a distinct per-item finding via `validateParentReferences()`: code `parent.missing-endpoint`, type `missing-parent`, carrying the lost parent id in `context.parentId` and a safe `parentId: null` proposed fix — `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`.
- **Promotion path exists.** `wl doctor dangling-parents [--apply]` detects dangling parents and detaches them (`parentId -> null`) — `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR), and `wl update <id> --parent null` detaches instead of writing `WL-NULL`.

The remaining defects are therefore narrower than the originally filed five ACs:

- **R1 — hard-delete admin paths still orphan children silently.** `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes each candidate via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`); `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` (`applyForeignItemCleanup`, `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`) likewise deletes each id individually and, although it cascades audit results and FTS entries, it neither cascades to nor refuses when an own-prefix child points at the deleted id.
- **R2 — promotion/detach loses the history.** `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply` contains no comment/attribution call, and neither `wl doctor --fix` nor `wl update <id> --parent null` records the previous parent or the rationale.
- **R3 — orphan reporting is not grouped.** Findings are emitted per child; there is no grouped summary keyed by lost-parent id carrying the count and child ids.
- **R3b — children of a *soft-deleted* parent are not reported at all.** `validateParentReferences` resolves `parentId` against `db.getAll()`, which includes soft-deleted rows (proved by `prune` filtering `status === 'deleted'` out of the same collection), so a soft-deleted parent looks resolvable. 9 of the 55 evidence orphans fell in this class.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every hard-delete admin path that can leave children without a resolvable parent (notably `wl doctor prune`; audit `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` and any other store-level `deleteWorkItem` caller) either cascades to descendants or refuses without an explicit opt-in, so no silent orphaning remains.
2. Any explicit orphaning opt-in (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment on each orphaned child naming the previous parent and the explicit decision.
3. `wl doctor` reports orphans as a distinct finding that includes the lost-parent id and the child id — including children whose parent is soft-deleted (R3b); `wl doctor dangling-parents --dry-run` summarises the grouped count of children per lost-parent id.
4. Promotion (`parentId -> null`, via `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, or `wl update --parent null`) records a comment naming the previous parent and the rationale (promote-because-live vs retire-because-stale), so the history is not lost.
5. The retention rule — promote when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is superseded, its target is gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered — is documented alongside the remediation path.
6. Automated tests cover: pruning a parent with children does not orphan them; explicit orphaning records the previous parent; doctor output names the lost parent and the children (including the soft-deleted-parent case); promotion clears `parentId`, keeps the children reachable, and records the comment.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (CLI/doctor docs and the remediation/retention guidance).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (now evidenced):** the 46-item hard-deleted batch came from a single-id hard-delete admin path — `wl doctor prune` is the leading candidate; `foreign-items --apply` can produce the same shape for own-prefix children.
- **Risk:** changing prune/foreign-items cascade behaviour could delete more than intended — mitigate with a dry-run-first default and an explicit opt-in for destructive cascades.
- **Risk (scope creep):** incidental doctor/delete cleanups discovered during the fix should be filed as separate items, not folded in.
- The delete-reason attribution defect is already fixed by **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) and is out of scope here; do not re-open or re-implement it.

## Constraints

- Do **not** re-implement already-shipped behaviour (recursive `wl delete`, the `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding, `--parent null` detach); build only the residual gaps R1–R3b.
- CHANGELOG is managed by the ship release pipeline, not this item.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` recursive-by-default with `--no-recursive` and `--reason` (`src/commands/delete.ts`; WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- `wl doctor` root `validate` includes `validateParentReferences()` → `parent.missing-endpoint` / `missing-parent` findings with a safe `parentId: null` fix (`src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`).
- `wl doctor dangling-parents [--dry-run|--apply]` detaches dangling parents (`src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts`, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR).
- `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`) — the residual orphaning route.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` hard-deletes with a "full cascade" limited to audit results + FTS entries (`src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`).

## Desired change

Close the residual gaps: make hard-delete admin paths cascade-or-refuse (R1), record the previous parent + decision whenever a child is orphaned or promoted (R2), and report orphans grouped by lost-parent id — including soft-deleted parents — in `wl doctor` output (R3/R3b), with a documented retention/remediation rule and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — cascade to descendants or refuse when pruning a parent that still has children.
- `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts` — same guard for `foreign-items --apply` when an own-prefix child points at a foreign id.
- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts` — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable; emit the grouped orphan finding (lost-parent id, count, child ids).
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — grouped orphan summary and comment-on-detach for `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — grouped count per lost parent in `--dry-run` and comment on detach in `--apply`.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — comment on each child when `--no-recursive` orphaning is applied.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — comment on `--parent null` detach naming the previous parent.
- `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — retention rule and remediation path.

## Proposed decomposition (plan input — not yet created)

Test-first ordering; each is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs):

1. **Orphan-guard failing test fixtures** (task, test-first) — shared fixtures for a hard-deleted parent, a soft-deleted parent, a foreign-prefix parent with an own child, and a promotion; tests assert the target behaviours and fail on current main.

> **Provenance:** this item is the ContextHub-home of SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E (`wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (t@t.com)`), moved per producer decision (2026-11-14): the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI, so the requirement record lives here and the SorraAgents tracking item was deleted. Producer answers on the three intake questions: **Q1 confirmed** — the sentinel/empty push refusal is absolute (fires even if the sentinel email hypothetically equalled the configured identity or an allow-list entry; policy forbids that state, pinned by SorraAgents `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`). **Q2 confirmed** — the guard covers both worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push AND `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`, the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite). **Q3 resolved** — tracked here in the ContextHub worklog; plan children live under this item and implement directly in this repository.

Planning is complete (`plan_complete`): see the plan-completion comment and the children. Full original brief follows verbatim.

# Intake Brief — wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E)

> Discovered-from: SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 (during the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS epic).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` quarantines *inbound* worklog commits authored by an incident-era sentinel identity (`t@t.com` et al.) — the author-identity gate — but nothing stops a checkout that still carries a sentinel `user.email` from *publishing* worklog commits under that identity in the first place. That is the 2026-10-22 incident (host `RossGameDev` pushed `T <t@t.com>`; every other clone refused to sync until the refs were re-authored by hand) and it recurred with two further inbound `t@t.com` commits on 2026-10-23 (`dec50d4d6`, `893203e8d`). `scripts/check_git_identity.py` detects the state but is advisory and fail-open (pre-push hook only) — a direct `wl sync` (as agent sessions run) has no guard, so the push side remains the durable gap.

## Users

- **Operators** syncing worklog data from any machine/checkout — a checkout with a stale sentinel identity (e.g. `RossGameDev`) must be stopped *before* it publishes.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl sync` to refuse to push when my checkout's identity is a sentinel, so I never strand worklog data for every other clone again.*
- **Agents** invoking `wl sync` directly in sessions — they skip the pre-push hook and currently have no protection.
  - *As an agent, I want the refusal to name the identity and the remedy, so I can fix `git config user.email` instead of shipping a poisoned ref.*
- **Every other clone/consumer** of `refs/worklog/data` — the pull-side gate keeps working, but prevention at the source means no more blocked syncs.
  - *As a syncing clone, I want sentinel-authored commits to never reach the remote ref, so my `wl sync` never refuses on inbound history again.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `wl sync` that would push worklog data while the effective `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel refuses *before* pushing, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`); the refusal applies when push would run (not with `--no-push` and not on the zero-change fast path).
- AC2 — The refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or to `syncAllowedAuthors` entries; the sentinel comparison is exact-email only (lowercased/trimmed match against the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`), never a wildcard/substring match.
- AC3 — An explicit escape hatch (`--allow-sentinel-author`) permits a deliberate one-off push, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`: it never bypasses the empty-email refusal and it is audit-logged in the sync output/log when used.
- AC4 — Regression tests cover the sentinel/empty/config-identity decision as a pure function (Cartesian over effective/configured email × allow-list) plus one CLI-level refusal test; no network.
- AC5 — Documentation: worklog sync docs describe the pull-side gate and the new push-side guard together (remedy, escape hatch, and why sentinels can never be allow-listed).
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub CLI suite for the new guard; SorraAgents suite remains green).

## Impact

Operators can no longer accidentally publish worklog commits under an incident-era sentinel identity, so every clone's `wl sync` stays mergeable and the manual re-authoring drill (2026-09-26, 2026-10-22, 2026-10-23) becomes unnecessary.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery:** the fix belongs in the **ContextHub worklog CLI** (TypeScript: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/...`, released as the `worklog` npm package), while this item is tracked in the **SorraAgents** worklog because the incident surfaced here. The implement workflow's worktree isolation is repo-scoped — the delivery mechanism (linked ContextHub/WL child item vs. cross-repo delivery directly from this item, cf. SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8) must be settled at plan time, *before* `implement.py start` (precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K kept this exact question open until planning).
- **Sentinel set parity:** reuse the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` rule from `scripts/check_git_identity.py` verbatim (duplicated in TypeScript — no cross-language import); keep both sets in sync via cross-referencing comments.
- **Escape-hatch symmetry:** `--allow-sentinel-author` mirrors `--allow-foreign-author` — never bypasses the empty-email gate, overrides config for that run only, does not modify `syncAllowedAuthors`.
- **No new dependencies; bounded, non-interactive; no network in tests.**

## Existing state

- **Pull side (guarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — `checkAuthorIdentity`/`enforceAuthorIdentityGate` refuse inbound commits whose author email is empty or foreign (allow-list `syncAllowedAuthors`, exact-email). Wired into `performSync` (`src/commands/sync.ts`) after the fetch, before any merge.
- **Push side (unguarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` commits the JSONL export with the ambient git identity and pushes to `refs/worklog/data`. `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite path) commits and force-pushes the same way. Neither checks the authoring identity.
- **Advisory guard only:** SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py` (owner SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) detects sentinel/empty/mismatched identities, fail-open in `.githooks/pre-push` — a direct `wl sync` (the agent-session path) bypasses it.
- **Policy:** incident sentinels may never enter `syncAllowedAuthors` — pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` (`test_incident_sentinel_emails_are_absent_from_the_project_allowlist`). Project allow-list: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local`, `sorra@thewizardscode.com` (`.worklog/config.yaml`).

## Desired change

1. In the worklog CLI, before the push step of `wl sync`, read the effective `user.email` (same identity git will commit with in the temp worktree) and refuse — with the identity named and the `git config user.email …` remedy — when it is empty or an exact sentinel match. Applies only when a push would actually run.
2. Pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (same input → same result for dry-run and normal modes): inputs = effective email, configured/expected email, `syncAllowedAuthors`, sentinel set; outputs = allow / refuse + reason. Guard order: empty → refuse unconditionally; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; otherwise pass (non-sentinel configured/allow-listed identities are never refused — exact-email rule, no wildcards).
3. New `--allow-sentinel-author` flag wired through `SyncOptions` → `performSync`; when used, the sync output and sync log record the bypass (audit trail).
4. Same guard applied to the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (force-rewrite path) so a sentinel identity can never author any worklog-data commit.
5. Regression tests: pure-function coverage of the sentinel/empty/config-identity matrix (unit, no network) plus one CLI-level refusal test (`wl sync` with a sentinel `user.email` refuses before pushing).
6. Documentation: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` updated to describe pull gate + push guard together; code comments cross-reference `scripts/check_git_identity.py` as the sentinel-set source of truth.

## Key Files:

- `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — add the pre-push identity guard to `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (and the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`).
- `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — add the sentinel set (`INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`) + the pure push-side decision function next to the existing pull-side gate (or a new `src/sync/push-authority.ts`).
- `ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — wire `--allow-sentinel-author` (option, `performSync` options, audit log output).
- `ContextHub/src/cli-types.ts` — `SyncOptions` typing for the new flag.
- `ContextHub/tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` and `ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — pure-function matrix + CLI-level refusal (no network).
- `SorraAgents/docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — document the push-side guard alongside the existing author-identity gate (AC5).
- `SorraAgents/scripts/check_git_identity.py` — canonical `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; cross-reference (source of truth for the TS set).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** (completed, high) — *Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era 'T <t@t.com>'* — owns `scripts/check_git_identity.py`, the advisory guard this item makes redundant-at-source.
- **SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC** (completed, high) — *Repair wl sync: allow operator GitHub identity, purge incident-era t@t.com commits* — established the pull-side allow-list/exact-email semantics this push guard mirrors.
- **SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits on refs/worklog/data* — discovery parent; the 2026-10-23 recurrence.
- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate* — 2026-10-23 second recurrence.
- **SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked: pi@local* — the epic this item was discovered during; `pi@local` allow-listing context.
- **SA-0MVVX9PAT009Q45H** (open, high) — *wl sync blocked: sorra@thewizardscode.com* — pull-side allow-list edge (deliberately allow-listed real identity — the carve-out pattern AC2 protects).
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** (completed, ContextHub store) — *wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills* — precedent for cross-repo items and for recording delivery-location as an explicit question before implement.
- **SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8** (completed) — *implement.py drive: refusal-aware finish recovery (cross-repo delivery record)* — precedent for delivering cross-repo work from a tracking item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AC2 interpretation (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** the sentinel/empty refusal is **absolute** — it fires even when the sentinel email also equals the configured identity or an allow-list entry. AC2's "never applies to the configured identity / allow-list" carve-out protects *non-sentinel* identities only (exact-match rule); project policy already forbids allowing sentinels (pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the two clauses do not overlap in any policy-compliant state. Guard order enforces this: empty → refuse; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; else pass.
- **Cross-repo delivery risk:** `implement.py` refuse changes outside the item's worktree; the fix must be delivered to the ContextHub repo through a linked item or cross-repo delivery. **Mitigation:** flag at plan time before `start`; record delivery mechanism as a decision in the work item.
- **Sentinel-set drift risk:** the TS set must stay byte-identical to `check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; no shared import exists across languages. **Mitigation:** cross-referencing comments + a unit test pinning the exact set (as `test_author_gate_allowlist.py` does on the SorraAgents side).
- **Escape-hatch abuse risk:** `--allow-sentinel-author` could be used routinely instead of fixing identity. **Mitigation:** audit-log the bypass in sync output/log (AC3) + docs frame it as incident-only, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "guard every git write in wl" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to the two worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push + doctor force-rewrite); track anything broader as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the effective `user.email` read at guard time is the identity git commits with — the temp push worktree shares the repo's config (including local overrides), so reading `git config user.email` from the repo root is sufficient. If a future git version allows per-environment author identity (env vars/`-c` overrides), the guard may need to consider `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`; out of scope today.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (AC2 scope — **CONFIRMED by producer**, 2026-11-14): "AC2 says the refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or `syncAllowedAuthors` entries. If a checkout's effective `user.email` IS an incident sentinel (e.g. the 2026-09-26 leaked-config state), must `wl sync` refuse anyway?" — **Recommended:** yes, refuse — the sentinel/empty gate is absolute and the configured-identity/allow-list carve-out protects only non-sentinel identities (guard order: empty → sentinel → pass). Rationale: sentinels are policy-forbidden from the allow-list (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the clauses never overlap in a compliant project; a literal carve-out would re-create the incident. Source: AC1 text (`user.email` set to a sentinel → refuse), `.worklog/config.yaml` policy comments, `check_git_identity.py` remedy text ("incident sentinels such as t@t.com never"). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q2 (push-path scope — **CONFIRMED by producer**, 2026-11-14): "Should the guard also cover `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite) or only the `wl sync` push step?" — **Recommended:** both — either path publishes worklog-data commits under the ambient identity and a sentinel-authored force-rewrite poisons the remote ref identically. Source: `src/sync/push.ts` structure (shared commit path). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q3 (cross-repo delivery — **RESOLVED by producer**, 2026-11-14: moved to ContextHub): "This SA item is the requirement/incident record, but the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI. Delivery mechanism?" — **Resolved:** this item IS the ContextHub WL record (moved from the SorraAgents store); plan children were recreated under this item and implement directly in this repository (worktree isolation now repo-aligned).
- Q4 (empty-email bypass — derived, no confirmation needed): "Does `--allow-sentinel-author` bypass the empty-email refusal?" — No: it mirrors `--allow-foreign-author`, which *never* bypasses the empty-email gate (documented in `src/commands/sync.ts` flag help and `src/sync/author-identity.ts`). Source: existing code, `--allow-foreign-author` semantics.

## Goal

Implementation slice for parent AC1/AC2: refuse to publish worklog-data commits when the effective git `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel, so a checkout with a stale sentinel identity can never poison `refs/worklog/data`. Covers the `wl sync` push path, the auto-sync/init callers of `gitPushDataFileToBranch`, and the doctor force-rewrite path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A TypeScript `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set (exact: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`; lowercased/trimmed comparison) plus a pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (inputs: effective email, configured/expected email, allowedAuthors, allowSentinelAuthor; outputs: allow / refuse + reason). # Hard-delete paths cascade-or-refuse (R1)

## Goal

Make hard-delete admin paths that can leave children without a resolvable parent either cascade to descendants or refuse — unless an explicit opt-in is provided. Closes residual orphaning gap R1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl doctor prune` refuses (or requires explicit `--cascade-children` opt-in) when a candidate item still has live children.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` audits its own-prefix children and refuses or cascades when a child points at the deleted foreign id.
- The dry-run-first default is enforced — destructive cascades require explicit opt-in.
- Regression tests verify no silent orphaning occurs through either path.
- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` documents the cascade-or-refuse behaviour.

## Key Files

## Goal

As an operator running the downtime dispatcher, I want a persisted Dispatcher
workspace / per-prefix tab anchor that no longer exists (herdr restarted, workspace
closed) to be **detected and re-provisioned automatically**, so that dispatch
self-heals after a herdr restart instead of silently refusing every candidate with
`anchor-unavailable` — leaving a 51-item backlog (plenty at `intake_complete` /
`plan_complete`) undispatched for hours with no visible cause.

## Reported symptom (measured 2026-11-15, ContextHub)

Intake and plan items are selected and nominated on every check-in
(`WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T`, `WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR`, …) but never dispatched. The claim is
taken, placement fails, the claim is rolled back.

`.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`, blocking `no-dispatch` reasons,
2026-11-13T23:33Z → 2026-11-15T00:56Z:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| **anchor-unavailable** | **124** |
| capacity-saturated | 40 |
| slots-unavailable | 35 |
| idle-window-spent | 20 |
| wl-error | 3 |

The live tick loop at the time of filing was `idle-age-qualified` →
`anchor-unavailable` → check-in re-offers → repeat (e.g. 00:56:04Z, 00:56:08Z).

## Root cause 1 — the persisted Dispatcher workspace is never validated, so the fallback can never recover

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`:

```json
{"paneId":"w6A:p1","workspaceId":"w6A"}
```

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` (written 2026-11-14T23:50Z):

```json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"}, ...}}
```

Workspace **`w6A` no longer exists**. Live `herdr workspace list` at filing:
`w52, w8, w4F, w3G, w5M, w50, w5S, w57`.

Verified by driving the real modules:

```
herdr pane get w6A:p5   -> {"code":"pane_not_found"}
herdr tab get  w6A:t2   -> {"code":"tab_not_found"}
listTabsInWorkspace(root, 'w6A') -> null
```

The failure chain:

1. `getDispatcherTabAnchor` (`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`) step 2 checks the
   cached pane with `isPaneAlive` → `false` → correctly falls through to
   re-provision. **The dead pane IS detected.**
2. Step 1 `ensureDispatcherWorkspace(deps)` does **not** validate the cached
   workspace: `readDispatcherWorkspaceId()` returns `w6A` verbatim and it is
   returned as the target workspace. A dead pane id is therefore converted into a
   dead *workspace* id, which nothing checks.
3. Step 3 `resolvePrefixTab` → `listTabs(w6A)` → `null` → `{status:'unknown'}`.
4. `unknown` fails closed by design ("never guess, never duplicate") →
   `getDispatcherTabAnchor` returns `null`.
5. `resolveDispatchPlacement` (`downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`) returns
   `{ok:false}`; the per-prefix resolver **deliberately never falls back** to the
   legacy `getDispatcherAnchor`. So `anchor-unavailable`, claim rolled back, and the
   next tick repeats it forever.

The two self-healing paths are mutually exclusive: the per-prefix resolver is the
one that is reachable and it cannot heal; `getDispatcherAnchor` (which *does*
self-heal — it checks pane liveness and re-provisions a fresh workspace) is
unreachable because the per-prefix resolver replaced it.

**Why nothing cleans it:** there is no reaper or TTL for either anchor file.
`persistPrefixTab` / `writeTabAnchors` / `writeAnchor` only ever write;
`readAnchor` / `readTabAnchors` validate the file *shape*, never that the referenced
workspace/tab/pane still exist. `WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER` added pruning for the
*coordination* file, not for anchors. Every herdr restart therefore leaves a stale
workspace id that permanently wedges placement for every prefix.

## Root cause 2 — the primary placement path cannot match this project's workspace (contributing)

`resolveProjectWorkspace` matches on the plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` only.
The ContextHub "Work Items" pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, not the
worklog root, so:

```
resolveProjectWorkspace('/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub', deps, <same>) -> null
```

Other roots match (AH, RISE, TCE, SA), which is why their panes dispatch and
ContextHub's does not. Because the primary path returns `null`, ContextHub falls
through to the wedged fallback in Root cause 1 — hence the total starvation. Fixing
Root cause 1 restores dispatch, but panes land in the Dispatcher workspace's `WL`
tab rather than the ContextHub workspace until this mismatch is also addressed.

## Proposed fix

**A. Validate the persisted workspace (the actual unblock).**

- `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` validates the persisted `workspaceId` still exists
  before reuse (`listTabs(<ws>)` parsed result, or `herdr workspace list`) and, when
  it is gone, provisions a fresh Dispatcher workspace and rewrites
  `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`.
- `getDispatcherTabAnchor` distinguishes **workspace missing** (recoverable →
  re-provision) from **herdr unreadable** (transient CLI error → fail closed, no
  duplicate workspace).
- Prune `byPrefix` entries that reference a dead workspace when rewriting the map,
  so stale ids cannot accumulate and mask later wedges.

**B. Diagnostics.** `anchor-unavailable` decision-log entries carry the detail
(missing workspace id vs unreadable CLI) so the next occurrence is diagnosable from
the log.

**C. Primary path.** Record the `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` mismatch as a diagnostic
decision entry, and document the operator remedy (start the plugin pane from the
worklog root). Whether to broaden the matching rule (ancestor/descendant match) is a
decision for plan time — a wrong-workspace match is worse than a fallback, so the
default is: do not change the matching rule in this item unless AC8 is satisfied
without ambiguity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Stale workspace self-heals.** With `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` and
   `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` pointing at a workspace that does not exist,
   `getDispatcherTabAnchor(cwd, deps, 'WL')` provisions a fresh Dispatcher workspace
   and returns a live anchor for a new tab — instead of `null`. Regression test
   reproduces today's exact state (`w6A` gone) against injected deps.
2. **Dead pane still heals.** The existing behaviour is preserved: a persisted
   prefix entry whose *pane* is dead (workspace alive) still re-resolves/re-creates
   the tab. Pinned by a test so AC1 does not regress the fast path.
3. **No duplicate workspaces.** A transient/unreadable herdr (`tab list` CLI error
   or unparseable output) still fails closed with `anchor-unavailable` and provisions
   nothing. Concurrent first-dispatchers (coordination lock + double-check) create at
   most one replacement workspace — test asserts `createWorkspace` is called once for
   two racing callers.
4. **Stale prefix entries pruned.** Rewriting the tab-anchor map drops `byPrefix`
   entries whose workspace id is the dead one; a test asserts the persisted file
   after recovery contains no `w6A`-style dead ids.
5. **End-to-end dispatch unblocks.** `resolveDispatchPlacement` returns `{ok:true}`
   in the reproduced stale-anchor state (test), and the occurrence no longer
   produces repeated `anchor-unavailable` decisions on consecutive ticks
   (orchestrator-level test with a stale anchor store).
6. **Diagnosable refusal.** When placement genuinely fails closed, the
   `anchor-unavailable` decision entry includes a machine-readable detail naming the
   failing boundary (persisted-workspace-missing vs herdr-unreadable), and a test
   asserts the field is present.
7. **Primary-path mismatch is visible.** A diagnostic is recorded when
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails to match a root whose plugin pane reports a
   different `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (naming expected vs actual), and the failure is
   documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` with the operator remedy.
8. **Matching rule unchanged unless unambiguous.** `resolveProjectWorkspace`'s
   match semantics are unchanged in this item. If plan chooses to add
   ancestor/descendant matching it must be covered by an ambiguity test (two panes
   claiming the same root resolve deterministically: focused first, then lowest pane
   id).
9. **Docs.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` placement section states: persisted
   anchors are validated against live herdr state on every resolution; a vanished
   workspace is re-provisioned once; an unreadable herdr still fails closed; and no
   anchor file has a TTL — recovery is on-read validation, not a reaper.
10. **No spawn/latency regression.** The validation adds no `wl` spawn (it reuses
    already-issued herdr calls); `fetcher-spawn-cap` / split-guard suites stay green
    and the refresh budget is unchanged.
11. **Full suite green.**

## Immediate mitigation (not the fix)

For the live machine, dispatch is wedged **now**; deleting
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` and
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` forces re-provisioning on the
next tick. Recorded so the operator can unblock before this item lands — the code
fix must make that manual step unnecessary.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` (no workspace validation), `getDispatcherTabAnchor` (`unknown` → `null`), `getDispatcherAnchor` (the self-healing path that is currently unreachable).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — `readDispatcherWorkspaceId`, `readTabAnchors`, `persistPrefixTab`, `writeAnchor` (write-only; no pruning, no validation).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `resolveProjectWorkspace` (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` only), `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — `resolveDispatchPlacement` precedence and the `{ok:false}` / `anchor-unavailable` verdict.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.anchor-resolvers.ts` — `defaultDispatcherAnchorResolver` / `defaultDispatcherTabAnchorResolver` / `defaultProjectWorkspaceResolver` (the deps that roll up the failures).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — existing anchor tests (stale-pane cases) to extend with stale-workspace cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.test.ts` (or nearest placement suite) — `resolveDispatchPlacement` precedence tests.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — placement / anchor documentation.

## Non-goals

- Adding a TTL or background reaper for anchor files — recovery is on-read validation.
- Changing the per-prefix-does-not-fall-back-to-legacy-anchor rule.
- Re-provisioning on a transient herdr read failure (that must stay fail-closed).
- Broadening `resolveProjectWorkspace` matching semantics without the AC8 ambiguity
  guarantee.
- Changing `send-to-pi.sh` / pane spawn behaviour, or the project-workspace tab
  placement policy for roots that do match.

## Decisions already taken

- **Validation over reaping.** A missing workspace is recovered on read, not by an
  age-based reaper: an anchor is stale because the thing it points at is gone, not
  because it is old.
- **Missing ≠ unreadable.** Only a positively-observed missing workspace triggers
  provisioning; an unreadable herdr keeps today's fail-closed behaviour.
- **One recovery mechanism.** Reuse `getDispatcherAnchor`'s existing
  provision-under-lock + double-check path rather than a second implementation.

## Related

- `WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC` — per-prefix Dispatcher tabs (introduced the resolver that
  replaced the legacy anchor and created this unreachable-healer situation).
- `WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN` — placement precedence (project workspace → per-prefix tab
  → legacy anchor) docs/tests this item extends.
- `WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG` — Dispatcher anchor origin (C0).
- `WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU` — Dispatcher placeholder root-pane adoption (same file
  family).
- `WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER` — coordination-file pruning precedent (a reaper for the
  coordination file; deliberately **not** mirrored for anchors).
- `WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9` — precedent: an un-timed failure path silently wedging the
  dispatch task.
- `WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T`, `WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR` — the prep-tier items repeatedly
  nominated and never dispatched in the reported window.

## Impact

A herdr restart can no longer silently wedge the downtime dispatcher: persisted
placement anchors self-heal on the next tick, so the backlog keeps moving and an
operator no longer has to delete anchor files to get work dispatched.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: a persisted Dispatcher anchor pointing at a dead herdr workspace wedges placement forever (anchor-unavailable) — validate on read and re-provision

---
# Goal

Add nice-value checking to `propose_remediations()` in `pressure_analysis.py` so renice actions are only proposed when the target process is not already at the desired priority.

## Background

`propose_remediations()` currently proposes renice for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In practice this meant:
- Processes already at nice 19 (max) would be proposed for no-op renice.
- Processes at nice 0 (default) would be proposed for +10 renice, potentially slowing live work (e.g. test suites).

The renice action in `actions.py` uses a default increment of +10. The target nice is therefore current_nice + 10. A renice is a no-op when current_nice >= 19 (the maximum).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: A new helper function `get_nice_value(pid, proc_root="/proc")` reads the nice value from `/proc/<pid>/stat` (field 19, kernel 2.6.22+) and degrades gracefully to `None` on failure.
- **AC2**: `propose_remediations()` calls `get_nice_value()` for each renice target. When the minimum nice value across all target PIDs is >= 19, the renice action is suppressed (not added to the actions list).
- **AC3**: When a renice action IS proposed, the `target` dict includes `"nice"` (int) and the `reason` string includes the current nice value, e.g. `"node consumes 3072 MB RSS (nice +10)"`.
- **AC4**: Unit tests in `tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` cover:
  - TC1: Process at nice 19 → renice suppressed (no renice action emitted).
  - TC2: Process at nice 0 → renice proposed with nice value in target/reason.
  - TC3: Multi-PID contributor where min(nice) >= 19 → all renice suppressed.
  - TC4: Multi-PID contributor with mixed nice values where min < 19 → renice proposed with min nice value.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — add `get_nice_value()`, modify `propose_remediations()`
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — add test cases TC1–TC4

## Risks

- Low: the `/proc/<pid>/stat` field layout is stable (nice is field 19 since kernel 2.6.22). Graceful degradation to `None` handles unreadable entries.
- Low: only affects renice proposals, not kill/prune/pace.
---

## Goal

As an operator, I want a bounded, documented grace window between claim and pane
visibility, so a hydrator tick that lands in the spawn→visible gap never releases
a live claim (parent root cause 3).

## Scope

Pin parent AC5 with an injected clock, both sides of the boundary:

- claim age < grace window, no pane visible yet → **no** release;
- claim age > grace window, no pane → today's release applies;
- the grace branch must NOT suppress the `in_review → completed` (audit tier) or
  `blocked` transitions — same precedence rule as the existing `held` signal;
- an item with no timestamps at all (legacy payload) is treated conservatively

- **Parent AC5** — **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock. — Delivered here as the grace-window tests asserting both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.

- A test asserts an item claimed 5 s ago with no visible pane is not released, using an injected clock (no real timers).
