## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the prep/audit-tier busy-signal contract pinned and the
duplicate-dispatch window closed by test, so nobody "fixes" the release by
re-introducing a claim-holder lock for prep tiers, and nobody re-opens the churn.

## Scope

Pin parent AC6 and AC7:

- AC7 (contract): a prep-tier dispatch (`/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`) has **no**
  `child-<id>.lock` claim holder, so pane evidence is the only signal. Assert the
  hydrator's `held` verdict is false for such an item and that the pane signal
  alone suppresses the release. The contract text lives in the `hydrator.ts`
  header comment (impl child) and is asserted here by behaviour.
- AC6 (no re-nomination): with the claim held and its pane live, the item is not
  returned to the dispatchable pool — it stays `in-progress` with the dispatcher
  assignee, so `wl next` / selection cannot nominate it on the next cycle. This is
  pinned in two layers: (a) drive a hydrate cycle against a cross-workspace pane
  and assert the item state is still claimed (item state, not just
  `demoted === 0`); (b) in `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts`, assert
  `evaluateCriticalFirstGuard` / the selection filters treat the claimed item as
  in-flight/held so it is not re-offered. Both layers are required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC6** — **No release storm / no duplicate dispatch.** After a dispatch, while its pane is live, the item is not returned to the dispatchable pool: a test asserts that a dispatched prep item is not re-offered/nominated on subsequent cycles while its pane exists (today it is re-offered every cycle). — Delivered here as the prep-tier tests plus the `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` nomination case.
- **Parent AC7** — **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen. — Delivered here as the prep-tier pane-only contract test and the `hydrator.ts` header contract text.

- A test asserts a prep-tier item (no claim-lock file) with a live cross-workspace pane is not released, and documents in-line that the claim-lock backstop does not cover prep tiers.
- A test asserts the item remains `in-progress` with a non-empty assignee after the hydrate cycle, i.e. it is not returned to the dispatchable pool.
- A test asserts that when the pane is genuinely gone the same item IS released (the pair proves the signal, not a blanket hold).
- A `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` case asserts the claimed item is not re-offered/nominated while its pane is live (the duplicate-dispatch window of parent AC6).
- No test relies on a real `flock`/`/proc/locks` read or a real `wl` spawn.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add cases to `hydrator.test.ts` (pane-only contract) plus, where cheap, a case
  in the downtime-worker selection/guard suite (`downtime-worker.gates.test.ts`)
  showing a claimed item is not offered.

- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` (read-only: the prep-tier gap)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` / `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` (nomination guard)

None (test-first).

impl child of WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (blocked-by the grace-window test child).

## Goal

As an operator, I want a bounded, documented grace window between a dispatch
claim and the first hydrator tick that could release it, so a tick landing in the
spawn→pane-title gap never releases a live claim.

## Scope (parent fix C, parent AC5)

- Reuse an existing recency signal, no new timestamp field: `wl list --json`
  already returns `updatedAt` and `activityAt`, so propagate them through
  `normaliseItem` into `HydratorItem` and derive the claim age as
  `now − max(updatedAt, activityAt)` (max = fail-open toward "recently active").
  The claim write itself (`wl update --assignee`) moves `updatedAt`.
- New bounded constant `HYDRATOR_CLAIM_GRACE_MS` (proposed default `120_000`,
  documented next to the other `HYDRATOR_*` budgets), overridable via a
  `claimGraceMs` option on `createHydratorRunner` / `HydratorDeps`.
- Settings surface (matching the existing `downtimeMarkerStaleWindowMs`
  pattern in `settings.ts`: default in `defaultSettings`, number-typed read with
  a clamp): key `hydratorClaimGraceMs`, wired in `worklist.ts` where the runner
  is created.
- Precedence: the grace branch behaves like `held` — evaluated **after**
  `in_review → completed` and `blocked`, and only suppresses the release to
  `open`. Ambiguity keeps the claim (parent decision "keep the claim on
  ambiguity"). Absent/unparseable timestamps: keep the claim for the window
  (documented, fail-open), pinned by test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC5** — **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock. — Delivered here as the grace-window tests asserting both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.

- An item claimed inside the grace window is never released, even with no pane visible (AC5 test child green).
- An item past the window follows today's rule exactly (AC5 test child green, both boundary sides).
- The grace branch never overrides `in_review → completed` or `blocked` (asserted by test; existing suite green).
- `normaliseItem` propagates `updatedAt`/`activityAt` and a missing/invalid value degrades to the documented fail-open direction.
- The grace window is configurable through the plugin settings key `hydratorClaimGraceMs`, clamped like the neighbouring settings, with its default recorded in `settings.ts` and the docs child.
- The release log line names the claim age and the window when a release is allowed past the window.

## Minimal Implementation

- `hydrator.ts`: `HydratorItem`, `normaliseItem`, constants, `runHydrationOnce` grace branch, `createHydratorRunner` opts.

## Goal

Make the persisted per-prefix tab-anchor map **self-pruning**: when the map is
rewritten for a (possibly new) Dispatcher workspace, drop every `byPrefix` entry
that cannot belong to that workspace, so dead workspace ids cannot accumulate
and mask a later wedge.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC4).

## Context

`persistPrefixTab` upserts one entry and keeps `{ ...current.byPrefix }`
verbatim, so entries pointing into a superseded workspace survive indefinitely:

```json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"},
                                "TCE":{"tabId":"w6A:t6","paneId":"w6A:p31"}}}
```

After a recovery to workspace `w6B` the map must not still carry `w6A:*`
entries: they can never resolve (the workspace is gone) and they make the
persisted state lie about where dispatch lands.

Herdr ids are workspace-scoped with a `<workspaceId>:` prefix (`w6A:t2`,
`w6A:p5`), so membership is decidable from the ids themselves — no CLI call is
needed and this stays a pure persistence-side change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistPrefixTab(dir, workspaceId, prefix, tabId, paneId)` writes a map
   containing only entries whose **both** `tabId` and `paneId` start with
   `<workspaceId>:` — plus the upserted entry (itself validated the same way).
2. An entry whose ids belong to a different (dead) workspace is dropped on the
   next write; the surviving same-workspace entries for other prefixes are
   preserved.
3. The map-level `workspaceId` is always the workspace being written (never a
   stale id).
4. **Stale prefix entries pruned.** Rewriting the tab-anchor map drops
   `byPrefix` entries whose workspace id is the dead one; a test asserts the
   persisted file after recovery contains no `w6A`-style dead ids (seeded from
   the recorded pre-fix map) and does contain the recovered workspace's entry.
5. Test: two prefixes in the same live workspace are both retained across a
   rewrite (pruning never drops a live sibling entry).
6. An ill-formed id (no `<workspaceId>:` prefix, e.g. a hand-edited file) is
   dropped rather than retained — it can never resolve in that workspace.
7. The write remains atomic (tmp + rename) and fail-closed (`false` on any
   error), exactly as today; no `wl`/herdr spawn is added.
8. Existing tab-anchor persistence suites stay green.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`: in `persistPrefixTab`,
  build `byPrefix` by filtering `current.byPrefix` on
  `tabId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`) && paneId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`)`
  before upserting; keep `writeTabAnchors` as-is (a `writeTabAnchors` caller that
  passes an explicit map keeps full control).
- Tests in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (persistence describe
  block) for AC2–AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — the prune rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — persistence tests.

## Dependencies

- `Test: pin healthy anchor paths` (tests first).
- `Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision` (AC4's post-recovery
  assertion runs through the recovery path).

## Out of scope

- Purging dead entries for workspaces that are still alive (only id-membership
  pruning is in scope here).
- Any TTL/reaper job; recovery remains on-read validation.

## Goal

Make the **primary-path near-miss visible**: when `resolveProjectWorkspace`
cannot match a worklog root but a herdr plugin pane reports a *different*
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, record a diagnostic naming expected vs actual — and
document the operator remedy — while **leaving the matching rule unchanged**.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC7 and AC8; parent "Proposed fix C").

## Context

`resolveProjectWorkspace` matches on the plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
only. The ContextHub "Work Items" pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` (the
plugin directory), not the worklog root `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, so:

```
resolveProjectWorkspace('/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub', deps, <same>) -> null
```

Other roots match (AH, RISE, TCE, SA), which is why only ContextHub fell through
to the wedged fallback. Fixing the stale-workspace bug restores dispatch, but
ContextHub panes then land in the `Dispatcher` workspace's `WL` tab rather than
in the ContextHub workspace — an invisible misplacement until it is logged.

### Plan-time decision (recorded)

The parent defers the question "broaden the matching rule?": **the rule stays
unchanged in this item.** Rationale: (a) parent AC8 explicitly makes broadening
conditional on an unambiguous ambiguity resolution, and two panes can legitimately
claim roots related by ancestry (this very project reports
`…/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, whose ancestor is the worklog root), so
ancestor/descendant matching would make ContextHub's own panes ambiguous;
(b) the item's user-visible unblock does not require it; (c) the operator remedy
is cheap and now documented. Broadening, if ever wanted, deserves its own item
with the AC8 ambiguity test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Primary-path mismatch is visible.** A diagnostic is recorded when
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails to match a root whose plugin pane reports a
   different `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (naming expected vs actual), and the failure is
   documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` with the operator remedy.
2. `resolveProjectWorkspace` reports the near-miss **only** when it returns
   `null` and at least one plugin pane reported a non-empty `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
   that differs from the wanted root: the record names the expected root, the
   actual `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, and the pane/workspace ids. Reporting is additive
   (an optional report callback or equivalent), so every existing caller and test
   is untouched.
3. No diagnostic is emitted when a match **is** found, or when the panes carry no
   `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` at all (an absent env is not a mismatch).
4. `resolveDispatchPlacement` records the mismatch as a `project-workspace-mismatch`
   diagnostic detail on the decision entry (expected vs actual), visible even when
   the fallback subsequently succeeds — i.e. a successful fallback placement still
   logs the mismatch.
5. **Matching rule unchanged unless unambiguous (parent AC8).**
   `resolveProjectWorkspace`'s match semantics are unchanged in this item: no
   ancestor/descendant or prefix matching is added, the existing ambiguity rules
   (two panes claiming the same root resolve deterministically — focused first,
   then lowest pane id) still hold, and every existing
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` test stays green with no behavioural change.
6. `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`'s doc comment states the
   rule is exact-root only, and that the reporting is diagnostic-only.
7. No new barrel export, no export-kind change (split guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`: collect per-pane
  `{ expectedRoot, actualRoot, paneId, workspaceId }` near-misses while scanning
  candidates; report them when returning `null` (via the optional callback added
  to the resolver signature); keep the match logic byte-for-byte identical.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: forward the
  mismatch record into the decision detail (`project-workspace-mismatch`),
  including when the Dispatcher fallback then succeeds.
- Tests: near-miss produces the record; a matched root produces none;
  missing-env produces none; existing ambiguity tests unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — near-miss reporting.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — record forwarding.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — resolver diagnostics tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — decision-entry test.

## Dependencies

- `Diagnosable anchor-unavailable refusal` (shares the placement-detail plumbing).

## Out of scope

- Any change to the matching rule, including ancestor/descendant matching
  (recorded plan-time decision above).
- Changing `send-to-pi.sh` or the project-workspace tab placement policy.

## Goal

Encode, **before the guard exists**, the regression contracts for a shared-build freshness check that runs once per test invocation: stale build, fresh build, missing build, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution. This is the test-first slice of the parent item (parent AC4).

## Scope

One unit suite, `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts`, driven entirely by temp-dir fixtures whose mtimes the test sets explicitly (mirroring `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`). No test may read this checkout's real `packages/shared`.

The suite targets the guard API the next child introduces: an injectable function that returns `null` when the run may proceed, or the actionable diagnostic string otherwise. Red-first evidence is collected by running the suite before the guard module exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` exists and builds every fixture in a temp directory with explicit `fs.utimesSync` mtimes, so assertions never depend on the real checkout's build state.
- Regression coverage in unit tests with temporary fixtures whose mtimes the test controls covers stale, fresh (equal mtimes), missing-dist, no-repo-root and worktree-resolution cases; the stale fixture is asserted red-first so the guard cannot pass vacuously (parent AC4).
- The five cases are exercised explicitly: stale (newest shared source mtime newer than the resolved build artefact), fresh (equal mtimes), missing `dist/`, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution (the resolved package is the main checkout's, not a worktree-local mirror).
- The stale case asserts the diagnostic names the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact mtime versus the newest source mtime, and the exact `npm run build:shared` rebuild command from that repository root.
- The missing-build case asserts the same actionable failure shape and does not expect a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- The no-repository-root case asserts the guard returns `null` (silent, fail-open) and never a false failure.
- The worktree case asserts the guard judges the resolved (main checkout) package rather than a worktree-local `packages/shared`, pinning the mirror-image false positive.
- Red-first evidence is recorded on this work item: the suite run against the absent guard fails, and the stale assertion is shown not to pass vacuously.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — new suite with controlled-mtime fixtures.
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture and mtime pattern to mirror.
- `./vitest.config.ts` — test discovery context (no change in this item).

## Test-first note

This item must merge before the guard implementation item; the guard item's acceptance requires this suite to turn green.

Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE.

## Goal

Provide the pure, injectable guard that decides whether the `@worklog/shared` build a run actually loads is at least as new as the newest shared source file, returning either `null` (proceed) or one actionable diagnostic naming the resolved directory, the mtimes, and the rebuild command.

## Scope

Implements parent AC1–AC3 at the helper level and turns the red-first suite from the sibling test item green. Resolution must mirror runtime module resolution (`node_modules/@worklog/shared`), not assumptions about the checkout layout. The repository root named in the message is derived from the resolved shared package (its `packages/` parent), so a linked worktree names the main checkout that owns the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guard resolves the `@worklog/shared` build through `node_modules/@worklog/shared` (following symlinks), so freshness is judged on the package the run actually loads and never on a worktree-local `packages/shared` mirror (parent AC2).
- The repository root used in the rebuild command is derived from the resolved shared package location, so a linked-worktree run names the owning checkout's `npm run build:shared`.
- Stale output returns one message naming the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact's mtime versus the newest shared source mtime, and the exact rebuild command `npm run build:shared` from that repository root (parent AC1).
- Missing build output (`packages/shared/dist` absent) produces the same actionable failure instead of a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from the first `@worklog/shared` import; when no repository root can be discovered the guard stays silent (fail-open, never a false failure) (parent AC3).
- An unresolvable package or an unreadable directory also degrades to `null` — silent and fail-open, never a false failure.
- Equal mtimes count as fresh, and generated or declaration files are excluded consistently with `isDistFresh`'s documented exclusion rule, or their irrelevance is justified in a code comment.
- The sibling suite `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` passes green, and `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` plus `isDistFresh`'s contract remain unchanged.
- A code comment states the mtime heuristic's trade-off (a branch switch or restored file can produce a false positive that costs one `npm run build:shared`) and that content hashing is deliberately out of scope.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/shared-dist-guard.ts` — new guard helper module.
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` — `newestMtimeMs()` / `isDistFresh()` precedent; do not change its contract.
- `src/cli.ts` — `sharedDistPreflight()` resolution-mirroring and diagnostic wording precedent.
- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — the suite this item turns green.

## Depends on

The red-first unit-test sibling must land first.

## Goal

Wire the shared-build freshness guard into every vitest invocation via `globalSetup`, so a run whose resolved `@worklog/shared` build is stale or missing aborts **before any test file executes**, with the actionable message and no side effects.

## Scope

This is the vertical slice that makes the guard observable end-to-end: configuration + runtime behaviour + verification evidence. It depends on the guard helper. The guard must run exactly once per invocation (`globalSetup`), never per test file (`setupFiles`), so it adds no filesystem walk to the 344 per-file setups.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `vitest.config.ts` gains a `globalSetup` entry alongside the existing `setupFiles`, pointing at the new setup module, and the guard executes exactly once per vitest invocation.
- Verified against a deliberately stale fixture checkout, the run aborts before any test file executes and prints the actionable diagnostic (resolved directory, mtimes, rebuild command) (parent AC1).
- All three `.pi/test-config.json` suite commands (`tests`, `packages/shared`, `packages/tui/extensions`) are shown to be covered by the guard, or a justified exception is documented.
- The guard performs no writes to the checkout: no implicit rebuild, and the working tree is unchanged after it fires.
- A fresh build proceeds silently, and an unresolvable package or undiscoverable repository root proceeds silently (no false positive) (parent AC3).
- The full project test suite passes with the guard wired in, after a legitimate `npm run build:shared` precondition; the verification run is recorded on this work item (parent AC7).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (parent AC7).
- End-to-end evidence (transcript of the stale-fixture abort and the fresh-build pass) is recorded on this work item.

**Key Files:**

- `./vitest.config.ts` — add the `globalSetup` entry.
- `tests/global-setup.ts` — new once-per-run setup invoking the guard.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — the three `suiteCommands` the guard must cover.
- `tests/shared-dist-guard.ts` — the guard helper called by the setup.

## Depends on

The shared-build freshness guard helper item.
